newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana's Rawlings heads for win in showcase poll.
newsitem.headline: Ghana's Rawlings heads for win in showcase poll.

text.p: President Jerry Rawlings outpolled his main challenger in Ghana's elections, making history as the first incumbent to be re-elected since independence in 1957.
In the process, his government also managed to stage the smoothest multiparty elections in West Africa, monitors said.
With more than two-thirds of expected votes counted on Sunday from Saturday's presidential and parliamentary elections, Rawlings took a comfortable lead with 53.2 percent of ballots.
His main challenger, John Kufuor of the opposition's Great Alliance, had 44.5 percent, according to the results from the National Election Commission.
In the parliamentary ballot held simultaneously, the president's National Democratic Congress party had 85 seats from the 200-seat assembly. The combined opposition had 50 seats.
The third contender, surgeon Edward Mahama of the People's National Convention, trailed with below three percent of votes.

The election commission put turnout at about 80 percent in the elections praised by foreign poll observers as the best organised in a region where logistics problems have marred voting in recent elections, often leading to violence.
"This is by far the best organised election I have seen in West Africa," said a Western monitor who has observed voting in three countries in the region recently.

Despite tension and some violence in the runup to voting, polling day itself passed off smoothly. In sharp contrast to acrimony that has marked each stage of recent elections in the region, Kufuor said he would gladly congratulate Rawlings when it emerged he was the winner.
"If this trend continues and I lose I will respect the traditional way," Kufuor told Reuters by telephone from his Accra home on Sunday.
Rawlings, a charismatic former air force pilot, twice seized power and ruled unchallenged for a total of 15 years before first seeking the popular mandate in 1992.
He is set to make history as Ghana's first re-elected leader. Since independence from Britain, all Ghana's elected governments have been toppled before serving out their terms.

Commonwealth and Organisation of African Unity observers have paid tribute to the organisation and conduct of the elections. "We believe that the conditions existed for a free expression of will by the electors," the Commonwealth team said.
Rawlings seized power as an air force flight-lieutenant in 1979, executing three former heads of state. He restored civilian rule but seized power again in 1981.
A former socialist firebrand, he embraced Western-style free-market economics, winning plaudits from the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.

The main opposition went into the 1992 elections in disarray and boycotted the 1992 parliamentary poll. Against the odds, Kufuor's New Patriotic Party and the People's Convention Party (PCP) formed a common front for this year's elections.
The PCP, which did not exist in 1992, follows the socialist line promoted by Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana's first president.
Kufuor, who celebrated his 58th birthday on Sunday, polled strongly in and around his stronghold of Kumasi, Ghana's second town and capital of the pre-colonial Ashanti empire.
